Passing of the cold front last evening marks the onset of cold air 
advection that is triggering lake cloud response off Lake Michigan 
with lake effect snow showers at the moment mostly confined to 
northern Lower Michigan. Northwest flow through today will maintain a
fair degree of lake clouds through today as temperatures this 
afternoon show limited recovery from the morning lows. High 
temperatures today expected to hold in the low-mid 40s. A secondary 
surge of cold air advection is expected this evening into tonight 
supported by a deepening trough axis over the Great Lakes. This 
trough will carry 850 mb temperatures down towards the -10C range and
bring a period of increased dynamics that will engage with the 
ongoing moisture flux off of Lake Michigan. This will lead to an 
uptick in lake effect precipitation later this afternoon and through 
the evening. Any precipitation that falls in the afternoon will lean 
towards a rain or rain/snow until lower level thermal profiles can 
cool enough to support a transition to mainly light snow showers. 
Forecast soundings point toward a brief period where there is 
saturation within the DGZ around 00Z. This occurs while the best lift
is below the DGZ layer and a relatively dry air airmass is 
maintained from around 2-3kft down to the surface. All of this will 
limit snow rates as the best dynamics move overhead in the 00Z to 06Z
time frame this evening. Minor accumulations may be possible as 
surface temperatures are expected to drop to freezing and then below
during the period of potential snow showers. Most favorable 
locations for any minor accumulations will mainly north of the I-69 
corridor, but scattered snow showers can be expected across most of 
southeast Michigan this evening into tonight. Temperatures will 
continue to plummet down into the mid 20s by 12Z tomorrow morning as 
thermal trough rolls through. 

Surface high pressure and mid level ridge will build over the region 
Tuesday into Wednesday. This will end lake effect snow showers by 
sunrise Tuesday and carry dry conditions through Wednesday. Coldest 
day of the week expected to be Tuesday with the thermal trough 
offering high temperatures that may struggle to reach 40 with most 
of the area holding in the 30s. Overnight lows Tuesday night will 
again fall into the low-mid 20s with a slight moderation in 
afternoon temperatures for Wednesday as the cold thermal trough 
shifts east. 

It appears likely that a stretch of wet weather is in store for 
Thanksgiving and Friday. This will come from a southern stream low 
pressure system drifting across the southern Gulf states that lifts 
northeastward phasing with a northern trough moving out of Canada and
through the Midwest triggering development of a Mid Atlantic low 
pressure system. Deeper moisture/precipitation will lift across 
southeast Michigan around this low starting Thanksgiving day. While 
precipitation looks likely, the uncertainty is in the details of 
precipitation amounts and p-type. This uncertainty comes from just 
how the southern stream wave interacts with the northern stream and 
the resultant placement surface low pressure development and 
associated forcing around it, which still has quite a bit of spread 
in the EPS. Long range forecast soundings point towards a very high 
DGZ up at 15-20kft and surface layer that is above freezing in the 
lowest 1kft. This would point towards a predominately rain event with
some potential for some melting snow to mix in for Thanksgiving with
a better chance to see snow Thursday night into Friday as lower 
level thermal profiles may cool down into the lower 30s. Similar 
story for Friday, though the DGZ may lower down to around the 10- 
15kft range. EPS 48 hour QPF totals ending 12Z Saturday have a roughly
60% to 80% chance across southeast Michigan to see a half inch or 
greater of QPF. Pattern stays active with another trough forecast 
swing through the Great Lakes over the weekend.
